findings.title: Pastoral freedom becomes a predation alibi
findings.claim: In the supplied pericope, permission to take Joseph into pasture and play under claimed guardianship meets the focus fear of wolf and eating, then returns as a ready-made account of what happened.
findings.mechanism: The focus {ar:يَأْكُلَهُ, tr:ya'kulahu, gloss:onu yemesi} names Joseph as feared prey, {ar:ٱلذِّئْبُ, tr:ez-zi'b, gloss:kurt} names the predator, and {ar:غَٰفِلُونَ, tr:ğafilun, gloss:habersiz} names the attention gap. The independent pasture, play, guarding, and racing terms in 12:12, 12:14, and 12:17 rearrange the permission request into a plausible predation script.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how the later alibi reuses the reassurance: open activity becomes distraction, guardianship becomes failed vigilance, and the wolf supplies the causal story.
findings.containment: The literal fear of a real wolf eating Joseph remains intact. This trusted channel nomination is bounded to the supplied pericope; it shows script-like reuse without claiming that the brothers' later account is thereby proved causally learned from the warning.

epistemic.reason: Trusted citable focus and pericope anchors supply the repeated lexical contacts and the pasture-to-alibi relation.
